data.exact_reserve_text: During the year, the Syndicate released GBP 9.5m of technical reserves in respect of prior years (2019: GBP 11.2m) arising from across the nuclear property and nuclear liability classes (2019: from across the nuclear property and nuclear liability classes).

named_events.loss_description: There has only been one significant core melt nuclear event paid by the insurance market, at Three Mile Island in the US in 1979.
Following the Fukushima accident in March 2011, an extensive review of the Syndicate's potential catastrophe exposure was undertaken.

named_events.event_name: Hurricane Andrew (spares warehouse on nuclear site)
named_events.loss_description: The largest insured windstorm loss to date was from a spares warehouse on a nuclear site from Hurricane Andrew in 1992... losses in the region of $200m, there was no damage to the nuclear unit.

data.standardized_narrative: The Syndicate opened 2020 with gross claims outstanding of GBP 35.941m. During 2020 the Syndicate recorded a prior-year reserve release of GBP 9.5m (a favourable development equal to ~26.4% of opening gross claims reserves), described as releases arising across the nuclear property and nuclear liability classes. The managing agent attributes the movement to favourable claims development across those classes rather than a single named event.
raw_causal_phrases: During the year, the Syndicate released GBP 9.5m of technical reserves in respect of prior years (2019: GBP 11.2m) arising from across the nuclear property and nuclear liability classes (2019: from across the nuclear property and nuclear liability classes).
We have received very few claims and those we did receive were settled at less than reserved.
The total property losses advised to date are within forecast loss expectancy.

gross_premium_mix.line_of_business: Fire and other damage to property

The claims development table (Note 18) is present and has been partially OCR-extracted but contains some OCR ambiguities; where cells were blank in the source, nulls are used.
